questions.question_html:
In film and videotape, it is possible to induce viewers to project their feelings onto characters on the screen. In one study, when a camera shot of a woman’s face was preceded by a shot of a baby in a crib, the audience thought the woman’s face was registering happiness. When the same shot of the woman’s face was preceded by a shot of a lion running toward the camera, the audience thought the woman’s face was registering fear. Television news teams must be careful to avoid such manipulation of their viewers.
Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?

A.text: A.Television news teams have abused their position of trust in the past

B.text: B.The expression on the woman’s face was, in actuality, blank.

C.text: C.A camera shot of a baby in a crib provoked feelings of happiness in the audience.

D.text: D.Audiences should strive to be less gullible.

questions.solution_html:
Solution

(c)
This is an inference question. The test writers are probably not interested in the conclusion of the passage. Considering the given options, we’ll look for a statement that seems so obvious that it almost doesn’t need saying.
• Television news teams have abused their position of trust in the past. If you chose this answer,
you inferred too much. The passage doesn’t say that news teams have ever abused their position
of trust. Eliminate it.
• The expression on the woman’s face was, in actuality, blank. The audience had no idea what
the expression on the woman’s face was, and neither do we.
• A camera shot of a baby in a crib provoked feelings of happiness in the audience. This is the
best answer. The passage says that the audience projects its own feelings onto characters on
the screen. If the audience believes the woman’s face reflects happiness, then that must have
been its own reaction.
• Audiences should strive to be less gullible. Rather it suggests Television news teams to be
careful to avoid manipulation of their viewers. This statement goes way beyond the intent of the passage.
Hence, option (c) is correct.

Consider the following statements regarding the process of evaporation from a water body and select the correct statement(s):

A.text: A.A decrease in atmospheric pressure facilitates evaporation.

B.text: B.Beyond a certain wind velocity, further increase in wind speed does not significantly increase evaporation.

C.text: C.Presence of dissolved salts increases the vapour pressure and hence increases the rate of evaporation.

D.text: D.Evaporation from a deeper water body is more during summers.

questions.solution_html:
Solution

(a, b)
• Presence of dissolved salts decreases the vapour pressure resulting in decreased evaporation.
• Evaporation from deeper water bodies is more during winters as compared to shallower
water bodies due to heat storage of water.

Gypsum is added to cement to counter the action of which of the following compounds?
questions.solution_html:
Solution

(b)
Gypsum present in the clinker of cement dissolves in water immediately and forms insoluble calcium sulphoaluminate. It deposits on the surface of C3A forming a colloidal membrane and consequently retards the hydration of C3A. It reduces the tendency of C3A to cause flash set in concrete.

questions.question_html: Which of the following statements related to cumulative toxicity in the environment is/are correct?

A.text: A.Bio accumulation and biomagnification can take place with heavy metals, pesticides and pharmacutical compounds.

B.text: B.Bio accumulation depends primarily on the uptake rate of pollutants from the environment and the rate of metabolism and excretion within the organism.

C.text: C.Easily degradable compounds generally do not show bioaccumulation and biomagnification.

D.text: D.Biomagnification is independent of trophic level and depends on the exposure concentration in the environment.

questions.solution_html:
Solution

(a, b, c)
Biomagnification depends precisely on trophic level. Higher levels accumulate more due to
consumption of contaminated prey, not just environmental exposure.

questions.solution_html:
Solution
